verdict: In its first quarter as the merged AvalonBay–Equity Residential giant, Vivmark booked a $747M GAAP loss on $544M of merger costs and stepped-up depreciation, even as Core FFO per share rose 5.1% to $1.03.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +56% vs AvalonBay alone a year ago (pre-merger)

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs +$0.96 a year ago — merger costs

kpis.label: Core FFO per share
kpis.note: +5.1% YoY — the cash measure, excl. merger costs

segments.name: Rental income
segments.note: Rent from the apartment portfolio. The jump is the merger: the quarter includes Equity Residential only from the August 17, 2026 merger date, while the year-ago figures are AvalonBay alone.

segments.name: Management & other fees
segments.note: Management, development and other fee income — a sliver next to rent.

opex.name: Depreciation
opex.note: Spreading the cost of the apartment buildings over their lives — it jumped because Equity Residential's assets were recorded at fair value in the merger, creating a much bigger base to depreciate. A non-cash charge.

opex.name: Transaction costs
opex.note: Deal costs of the AvalonBay–Equity Residential merger, expensed in the quarter it closed.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — includes about $80M of merger-related compensation costs.

opex.name: Property management
opex.note: The cost of managing the communities day to day.

opex.name: Development & pursuit costs
opex.note: Development and pursuit costs expensed rather than capitalized.

opex.name: Casualty & impairment
opex.note: Casualty and impairment losses on properties.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $124M and a $6M loss from unconsolidated investments, partly offset by a $108M gain on sales of communities, $11M of other income and $4M of non-operating gains.
follow100Note: This was a loss quarter: merger costs and non-cash depreciation were far larger than the quarter's rent profit, so the 'kept as profit' row is negative — the loss was covered by the combined company's balance sheet.

takeaways.title: The merger bill drove the loss
takeaways.text: Merger-related costs of $544M — $464M of transaction costs plus about $80M of merger compensation inside G&A — cost $0.92 per share. Excluding them, Core FFO per share rose 5.1% to $1.03.

takeaways.title: Depreciation is a merger artifact
takeaways.text: Depreciation nearly quadrupled to $898M because Equity Residential's communities were stepped up to fair value on the merger balance sheet. It is non-cash, and FFO adds it back.

takeaways.title: The apartments themselves did fine
takeaways.text: On a merged same-store basis — both legacy portfolios as if combined all along — revenue rose 2.4% and NOI 1.7% at 95.8% occupancy.

oneTimers: Merger-related costs of $544M ($0.92 per share): $464M of transaction costs plus roughly $80M of merger-related compensation in general & administrative expense. The company now expects total merger-related costs of about $725M.
Depreciation of $898M reflects the fair-value step-up of Equity Residential's assets in merger accounting — a non-cash charge that will stay elevated.

sources.label: Q3 2026 supplemental with consolidated statements (SEC EDGAR)

footerNote: Vivmark Residential was formed on August 17, 2026 by the merger of Equity Residential and AvalonBay Communities, accounted for as a reverse acquisition: year-ago comparatives are AvalonBay alone, and this quarter includes Equity Residential only from the merger date. Direct costs are property operating expenses ($245M) plus property taxes ($147M). Net loss attributable to controlling interests was $735M; the net loss available to common shares was $736M.
